canonical_statement: Find the optimal constant $c>0$ such that the following holds. For all sufficiently large $N$, if $A\sqcup B=\{1,\ldots,2N\}$ is a partition into two equal parts, so that $\lvert A\rvert=\lvert B\rvert=N$, then there is some $x$ such that the number of solutions to $a-b=x$ with $a\in A$ and $b\in B$ is at least $cN$.

must_determine: The requested value, class, function, order of growth, optimal constant, or necessary-and-sufficient criterion—whatever the canonical statement asks to determine—without leaving a residual parameter family.
Both sides of every extremal claim: a construction/lower-side witness (when applicable) and a matching obstruction/upper-side proof establishing optimality or exactness.
Every subquestion or explicit “in particular” target in the canonical statement, unless the source itself formally declares that only a named subpart is the target.
A proof that the stated answer has exactly the required quantifier scope, endpoint conventions, and full-sequence/asymptotic meaning.

Reviewer-mandated close condition: close_branch_A: must_determine does not name the actual target object for THIS problem. It should explicitly require: the exact value (or proven-optimal characterization) of the largest admissible c, together with both a construction achieving the matching upper side (partition families showing no larger c works, i.e. an upper bound construction for M(N)/N) and a lower-bound proof (every balanced partition has overlap ≥ cN eventually). As written, a close supplying only an improved lower bound record (e.g. beating 0.379005) would superficially satisfy 'the requested value… optimal constant' language without being a determination.

Reviewer-mandated close condition: close_branch_A: the canonical statement does not ask for the value of the Lean file's primary target (the limit of MinOverlapQuotient) — but the source's open variant erdos_36.variants.upper shows a second distinct constant (limsup side). The contract must state explicitly which clauses of the source are covered by the canonical text so a close cannot be credited for resolving only the liminf-side constant while the campaign silently treats the limsup/limit variants as resolved or vice versa.
close_branch_A.statement: DETERMINATION CLOSE: answer the canonical determination problem completely, over the entire stated parameter domain, with an explicit value/classification/asymptotic law or a theorem giving necessary-and-sufficient conditions.

definitions: Formal-semantics guard: any Lean or equivalent formalization used in the campaign must be semantically bound back to this canonical statement. Types, endpoint conventions, and degenerate cases may not be guessed; any formal/prose mismatch must be resolved explicitly before claiming closure.

Quantifier-order guard: the quantifiers occur in the order stated and may not be commuted, weakened, or replaced by sampled cases. Salient source phrases include: For all sufficiently large $N$; all sufficiently large $N$.
Partition guard: preserve whether parts/classes are ordered, disjoint, exhaustive, nonempty/equal-sized, and whether the partition is of vertices, edges, integers, or another object.

Extremal guard: minimum/minimal and maximum/maximal are different notions. When a numerical extremum is requested, a close needs both an attaining construction/witness (or exact existence) and a proof that no better value is possible.
Threshold guard: every “at most/at least/more than/less than” boundary is literal; strict and non-strict inequalities and integer rounding may not be interchanged.

Review-authority rule for this repaired contract: the immutable canonical_statement is the controlling mathematical target. Where a reviewer defect identifies an exact source/Lean encoding as the intended convention, that exact encoding is binding; any alternative convention mentioned only to expose ambiguity is forbidden unless exact equivalence to the controlling target is proved.

Binding semantic repair: definitions: the load-bearing quantity is never defined. The canonical statement's 'number of solutions to a-b=x with a∈A, b∈B' must be pinned as the count of ORDERED pairs (a,b)∈A×B (the Lean Overlap definition), with a,b integers, A,B subsets of ℤ (not ℕ), and the maximum taken over all x∈ℤ (including negative x, since a-b can be negative). Without this, 'at least cN' is ambiguous and a close could silently count unordered pairs or restrict x to nonnegative values.

Binding semantic repair: definitions: 'optimal constant c>0' is undefined. The property 'for all sufficiently large N, every equal partition has some x with overlap ≥ cN' is monotone downward in c, so the 'optimal' constant is a SUPREMUM over admissible c (namely liminf_{N→∞} M(N)/N in the M(N)/N normalization of the Lean file); the source variants (Scherk/Świerczkowski/Haugland/White lower bounds, MRS/Haugland upper bounds) confirm this reading. The contract must state whether a close must (i) exhibit c with the property and prove the property fails for every c > c*, or (ii) prove the supremum is attained, and must pin the normalization 'number of solutions ≥ cN' against the Lean's M(N)/N = MinOverlapQuotient. A close asserting a candidate value without specifying attainment vs. supremum semantics would be unverifiable.

Binding semantic repair: definitions: 'sufficiently large N' is left unpinned: a close may choose its own threshold N₀, but the contract must state that the constant c is independent of N and of the threshold, and that the quantifier is ∀N≥N₀ ∃ per-partition (not ∃N₀ with c depending on N₀, and not 'infinitely many N'). The known_traps list covers this generically but the definitions field never fixes the c-vs-N₀ dependency for THIS statement.

Binding semantic repair: definitions: the partition guard does not record that {1,…,2N} here means the integer interval [1,2N]∩ℤ of size 2N, that both parts have cardinality exactly N (not ≤ N), and that A and B are unlabeled (the overlap symmetric under swapping A,B up to negating x) — a reformulation fixing an order or allowing unequal parts would be a silent relaxation.

invariants_that_must_survive_every_refor: The canonical statement text is immutable; every proof target must imply exactly that statement (or its literal negation for a negative close).
Every quantifier, domain, hypothesis, strict/non-strict inequality, endpoint, normalization, and parameter dependency survives every reformulation.
Discrete structure is preserved: integrality, distinctness, ordering, multiplicity/set-vs-multiset conventions, and exact cardinalities may not be relaxed silently.
Any asymptotic/eventual claim retains the same limiting variable and full-sequence requirement.
The extremal direction and the distinction between minimal/maximal and minimum/maximum.
known_traps: QUANTIFIER SLIP: exchanging ∀ and ∃, moving an epsilon/constant after the limiting variable, or replacing “all sufficiently large” by “infinitely many”.
SAMPLED-TO-UNIVERSAL: checking many finite instances and promoting the observation to an unrestricted theorem without a valid finite-reduction theorem.
DOMAIN DRIFT: proving a translated/scaled/relaxed version without an exact map back to the original domain, endpoints, and discrete constraints.
STRENGTH CONFUSION: refuting a stronger folklore conjecture does not refute the canonical claim; proving a weaker statement does not prove it.
BOUND-AS-ANSWER TRAP: an improved record bound or candidate constant is not a determination unless matching lower/upper (or necessary/sufficient) proofs establish exactness.
non_results: A theorem for only a selected finite set of parameter values when the statement is uniform or asymptotic.
A result only on a favorable subsequence, density-one subset, almost-everywhere set, or “generic” family when the canonical statement requires the full sequence/all objects.
A numerical fit, heuristic, Monte Carlo result, floating-point experiment, or finite computation without a proved finite-reduction/transfer theorem to the canonical claim.
A restricted-family result obtained by adding hypotheses not present in the statement, unless those hypotheses are proved without loss of generality for every canonical instance.
A conditional theorem whose decisive premise is an unproved conjecture of comparable strength.
A reduction to an equivalent-strength open problem, a tautological rephrasing, or a definition of the requested answer in terms of the original unresolved predicate.
A continuous/real-valued/LP/SDP relaxation without a proved integrality or exact-transfer theorem when the canonical objects are discrete.
A stronger-looking statement in a different normalization/domain that does not formally imply the canonical statement.
Any isolated improved upper or lower bound that does not determine the requested value/order/classification.
A conjectured optimal constant/exponent/class based on computation without matching achievability and impossibility proofs.
Declaring the residual cases “open” instead of resolving them or proving genuine independence.
A feasible construction or a bound on the extremal value without the complementary proof showing optimality/exact extremality.

Explicit non-result: non_results: the source contains an existence-of-limit theorem variant (erdos_36.variants.exists: the limit exists and is < 0.385694). The contract does not record whether proving mere existence of the limit, or bounds on the limsup side, count toward or are orthogonal to the close. A close could smuggle in 'the limit exists and lies in [0.379005, 0.380927]' — a confinement, not a determination — and the contract's non_results list does not explicitly exclude 'interval confinement without exact value' or 'existence-of-limit without value' for this problem.

Explicit non-result: non_results: missing explicit exclusion of 'improved limsup upper bound only' (e.g. beating 0.3809268…) as a fake close: since the canonical constant is the liminf-side constant, an upper-side limsup result alone does not determine it, and this near-miss is not listed.
permitted_background: Definitions and elementary facts in the named mathematical domain, with every imported theorem used only under its exact published/formal hypotheses.

Standard algebraic, combinatorial, analytic, probabilistic, number-theoretic, set-theoretic, and asymptotic lemmas needed to manipulate the objects appearing in the statement; no theorem equivalent in strength to the target may be assumed.

Exact finite computation, SAT/SMT/MILP, interval arithmetic, symbolic algebra, exhaustive enumeration, or custom verified tooling may be used as a lemma/certificate when its finite search space and transfer to the unrestricted claim are proved.
Lean/Mathlib or another proof assistant may certify intermediate and final results; kernel acceptance does not by itself excuse a semantic mismatch with the canonical statement.
Standard proved facts about primes, divisibility, congruences, multiplicative/additive functions, and elementary/analytic number theory may be used with explicit dependency and range conditions.
